what_was_done: The three path-taking git calls in _flush_locked (add -A, rm --cached, commit --only) now run with GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 in their env (module constant _LITERAL_PATHSPECS), so a record name's glob characters and a leading ':' are never read as a pattern; the env form keeps the commit's -c options position-free. Verified the new test fails with the env blanked (scratch pytest plugin): without the fix the rejected a.md rides into HEAD through the '[ab].md' pathspec. New test test_flush_does_not_commit_a_rejected_neighbour_of_a_glob_name: over-cap a.md beside a valid [ab].md — flush is partial, a.md named with over_cap, [ab].md committed, a.md absent from HEAD and still in status. test_flush_commits_a_renamed_name_with_space_and_accents is now a real rename (nächste Runde.md -> über nächste Runde.md committed, then renamed): both paths committed, old name gone from HEAD, tree clean, next flush clean — it exercises the rm --cached staging too. Spec: topics/state-commits.md step 4 now says the path-taking git calls run with literal pathspecs and why.

The seam attribute is named: StoreBusy.released for the entries released, and lock_release now also attaches StoreBusy.kept for the entries held back because their run_end was busy (locks.py). The lock_release docstring no longer says a caller cannot distinguish busy from nothing matched — it says the exception is how a caller tells them apart and names the kept entries. hooks/liveness.py._released_under_busy reads 'released' (the rename was landed by the hook-runner-b builder in this tree while this fix ran; verified in place and aligned tests with it). Cross-unit test test_session_end_logs_released_entries_when_a_run_end_is_busy: two entries of one session, first run_end succeeds, second is busy, real lock_release through liveness.release with a stub ctx — it returns the first entry, logs exactly one lock.released for its run, logs runner.liveness_error, and leaves the kept entry with its run live; verified it fails when _released_under_busy reads 'entries' again. test_release_logs_a_busy_store's fake StoreBusy now carries 'released'. Spec: topics/state-api.md names StoreBusy.released and StoreBusy.kept as the seam's contract and says the session-end caller logs the released entries as lock.released. Still open for the orchestrator: the same one-clause naming in plan records.md 3 and hook-runner-b.md 4 (rewrite/plans/ is not mine to edit).

cmd_lock._run tells the two StoreBusy causes apart by the exception's kept attribute, which lock_release attaches only when an entry was kept because its run_end was busy (a bare lock.flock timeout from store.locked carries no attributes). Flush case: error 'a flush is running; the release could not end the runs...' and holder is _names(kept[0]) — the entry actually kept, taken from the exception, no longer lock_entries()[0], which could be an unrelated session's entry. Flock case: error 'the run lock is busy; another release or a survey holds it — retry shortly', holder null, released empty — 'flush' appears in it nowhere. New test test_cmd_lock_release_while_the_run_lock_is_held holds lock.flock from another process: 'lock release --force' exits 1 inside the wait (asserted under 4 s), says the run lock is busy, never 'flush', names no holder, and leaves lock.json and the live run untouched; with the lock free the same command exits 0. The existing flush-held test continues to pass and names the kept entry. Spec: commands/lock-release.md 'Output and failure cases' states both busy shapes.
